optimize_reason: Cash-flow-on-assets trend. Operating cash flow is the profitability measure least exposed to cross-jurisdictional accounting policy: depreciation useful-life assumptions, revenue-recognition timing and tax treatment all differ between US GAAP, IFRS and J-GAAP, and those differences are exactly where the current EBIT-on-assets champion loses its EMEA and APAC Sharpe. Economics: a firm generating more cash per unit of asset base than a year ago is gaining genuine operating efficiency, and the market reprices this only gradually.

Asset-turnover trend (revenue over total assets). This is a pure operating-efficiency quantity that carries almost no accounting-policy content - revenue and the asset base are recognised similarly across regimes - so it should behave far more uniformly across AMER, EMEA and APAC than any earnings-based measure. Economics: improving revenue generated per unit of assets means the firm is sweating its capital base harder, a real competitive gain that is priced in gradually.

Champion with the widest possible cross-sectional benchmark (whole market) while keeping subindustry risk neutralization. Benchmarking against the entire market maximizes the retained industry-level dispersion and gives every region a fully populated book, which is the direct lever on the failing EMEA and APAC regional Sharpes.

Champion with platform neutralization widened to MARKET instead of SUBINDUSTRY. Widening the risk neutralization at platform level while keeping the sector benchmark inside the expression changes the residual exposure profile and raises cross-sectional dispersion, aiming to lift overall Sharpe toward the 1.95 level at which cluster-test warnings disappear on their own.
